$comment: The canonical enumeration of this framework's source material and its standards series. AUTHORED AND REVIEWED BY HAND, then frozen. scripts/inventory.mjs extracts from the sources and compares its result AGAINST this file; it must never regenerate it. A parser that becomes more or less forgiving can then only disagree with this file, and disagreeing fails the build. Regenerating this from a run would destroy the entire guarantee.

sources.role: domain — which standards exist, which prohibitions exist, what an analysis must disclose

sections.heading: (preamble)
sections.note: The mode taxonomy, introduced by the line 'Distinguish:'. It sits before the first heading, so a heading-driven scan would miss it entirely.

sections.heading: Required standards
sections.note: Introduced by 'Cover:'. One standard per bullet, in source order, numbered 02 through 24.

sections.heading: Must-never rules
sections.note: Introduced by 'Never:'. All 23 are reproduced verbatim in Standard 25 and each becomes a forbidden-level rule in rules/prohibited.json. The exact text is recorded here so that softening one — 'never describe' becoming 'avoid describing' — fails the build rather than passing review.
bullets: compare values from different time periods without accounting for relevant differences
recommend an investment solely because its price recently increased
present a single forecast as certain
use excessive precision in long-term projections
optimize investment returns while ignoring required liquidity
recommend risk without considering time horizon
treat mathematically optimal as automatically personally appropriate
encourage borrowing for investment without explicit risk analysis
present tax estimates as exact when important information is missing

sections.heading: Uncertainty
sections.note: Introduced by 'Where appropriate include:'. The section's two prose statements are not bullets and are recorded under prose below: projections should use scenarios or ranges where uncertainty materially affects the answer, and these four must never be implied to exhaust possible outcomes.

prose.heading: Deliverables
prose.note: Four statements, no bullets. Each is a cross-cutting requirement rather than a topic, which is why they become standards 26 through 28 plus a plan obligation rather than one standard each.
statements: Implement standards, prohibitions, applicability, evidence requirements, verification, tests, documentation, and examples.
Automatically verify financial mathematics where feasible.
Clearly identify what requires current external data or personal financial context.
Run all validation and report results.

sources.role: system — how the standards are represented, evaluated, evidenced, and protected

sections.heading: (preamble)
sections.note: The fifteen candidate concepts, introduced by 'At minimum, investigate whether the repository needs concepts equivalent to:'. The directive is explicit that these must not be implemented merely because they are listed, and that the reasoning must be documented — so every one of them is dispositioned in artifacts/adr/0005-concept-disposition.md. This section was MISSED when the inventory was first authored by hand and was caught by scripts/inventory.mjs disagreeing; the guard earning its place on its first run is the reason it is written before any standard rather than after.

sections.heading: AI usage
sections.note: Two bullet lists in one section: the ten capabilities an AI operator must have, then the five conclusions it must be able to reach. The extractor collects both under this heading, which is why the declared list below runs to fifteen.
bullets: initialize the standards against a target project
refuse or stop work that would violate an invariant
update evaluations when relevant project state changes

sections.heading: Repository quality
sections.note: The production-software obligations this repository holds itself to.

prose.heading: Standards integrity invariant
prose.note: Reproduced verbatim in Standard 29 and encoded as the non-exemptible rule integrity.no-weakening.
statements: A human or AI must never bypass, weaken, remove, reclassify, reinterpret, falsify evidence for, or manipulate a standard, test, applicability determination, evidence requirement, or verification mechanism solely because it prevents the desired implementation or conclusion.

$standardsComment: One standard per source unit. `coversSource` names the unit each standard answers for, so a reader can trace any requirement back to the text it came from, and so a source bullet with no standard is visible as a gap rather than as an absence.
